params.body:
The designer's second delivery (maquette of 15 September, plus Newsreader) applied to the whole site.

## What the maquette fixes

- **Three typefaces, three roles.** Newsreader for what tells (headlines, card titles, the italic first word of a section), Array for what counts (the numbers, the momentum, the stamp word in a heading: "Latest **Trends**", "**Youth culture.**"), Archivo for what operates. Read straight from the pdf's embedded fonts; Array is the dot-matrix face the site already shipped.
- **The palette**, measured from the pdf: white paper, stone cards without a border, one green (`#416E68`) for the button and the logo, coral (`#EF522D`) for the part that moves, mint for soft panels, night only for the reports band.
- **The hero**: pages 1 and 2 of the draft are two home pages. Shane chose page 2 ("feels editorial"): the collage left, a mint panel right that is the navigation on the home page (the pages in serif capitals, the logo in white, the two calls, the intro), so the home page carries no bar above it. Trends as rows, with the evidence and the momentum. Page 1 (strip under the nav, cards) is in the history as the first commit; its strip still serves the prelaunch screen and the share image.

## What follows from it on every page

- Nav: pages left, the full green logo centred, sign in and the green block right. On a phone the menu is the mint panel from page 4 of the maquette, big serif capitals.
- Footer: green, with the same serif menu.
- Trend card (on /trends and in the reading room): stone, eyebrow, serif title, coral groove, dot momentum, a black-and-white piece of the collage underneath. On the home page the trends are rows.
- Post card: image, text on mint, a green bar with the date and the call.
- Sub-page heads: page 3 of the maquette, mint headline over the grey collage.
- Buttons are square (`.btn`); secondary calls are `.cta`. No pills anywhere.
- The reports band (home and /reports) is the one dark surface.
- The share image and the mail theme follow the palette; the mail wordmark PNG is green now.

## Assets

- `Newsreader-60.woff2` and `Newsreader-Italic-60.woff2`: optical size pinned to 60 (the designer set everything in 60pt, also the card titles), weight 300 to 700, Latin subset, 58 and 65 KB. Array Wide removed, nothing used it.
- `hero-split.*` (1400 wide, avif/webp/jpg) cut from the full collage delivered in August for the home page; `hero-strip.*` and `hero-strip-tall.*` for the prelaunch screen; `band-numbers.*` a blurred, green-tinted cut for the numbers band. `hero-cut.*` removed.
- Green logo variants: fill only, shapes untouched.

## Tests

276 pass (this replaces #117, which failed on one host-bound assertion of the new hero test). Three moved with the design: `HeroCollageTest` (the split hero on the home page and no second nav above it, the strip on the prelaunch screen, the preload), `IconsTest` (Newsreader, Array and Archivo must be in the build), `OneVoiceTest` (the nav's responsive logo pair counts as one). Pint, ESLint and `bin/lint-tailwind` clean.

## Decided here, for the designer to confirm (also in BRAND.md)

- One green: the wordmark measured `#3A6760`, the button `#416E68`; treated as one swatch converted twice.
- The mint panel has no sign-in in the draft; a small one sits under the calls, a member has to get in somewhere. The call in dark green on mint is as drawn, 4.0:1.
- Sub-page heads use page 3 of the maquette; the ticker is a light band with a coral dot; the sections the maquette does not draw (how we read, the graph, why Gentells, pricing teaser, newsletter) are set in the same language.
- The "Explore all trends" pill at the bottom of page 1 is a screenshot of the old site pasted in as a placeholder (image 11 in the pdf), not followed.
params.title: The site in the designer's second delivery: Newsreader, Array, the split hero
